brief: US composite PMI rose from 56.0 to 58.4 in September, the fastest expansion since July 2021, but the report's input costs gauge hit its highest level since October 2022. That strength, hawkish remarks from Fed Governor Barr, and a weak 5-year Treasury auction (the lowest bid-to-cover since 2018) pushed yields sharply higher. The 10-year hit a 19-year high of 5.10% and the 30-year reached 5.40%, a level last seen in 2004. Markets are now pricing roughly four more Fed hikes. Raymond James thinks that overprices what the Fed will deliver and expects yields to trend lower over the next 12 months. Large-cap equities have mostly shrugged off the yield jump, with the S&P 500 sitting 1.2% below its record high, but breadth is weak underneath: 9 of 11 sectors are negative month-to-date and the Russell 2000 is 7.5% below its high, so RJ expects market leadership to stay narrow until yields stabilize. Separately, Democrats' odds of winning the Senate hit a cycle-high 66% on Polymarket amid an expanding national polling lead, and the administration is reportedly weighing a 90-day diesel export ban after diesel prices hit a record near $6.50 per gallon.
